When writing nested CSS rules, a selector like `:hover` without the nesting reference (`&`) applies to descendants rather than the element itself. Since `:hover` was added directly inside `root>mid>leaf`'s CSS block without `&`, hovering the leaf node itself does not trigger the style. Therefore, you must edit `root>mid>leaf`'s own CSS block to include `&` so that the hover selector correctly targets the leaf node.

ANSWER: root>mid>leaf
